title: Split Loop

solutions.title: Two loops, one for each total
solutions.tradeoff: A second pass over the same array of orders, and two named sums to maintain instead of one loop - a cost worth paying the moment either total needs to change, be tested, or be read on its own for a reason the other one doesn't share.

reviewFocus: Does each of the two loops read exactly one field off `order` - `totalCents` in one, `flourGrams` in the other - or did stripping the duplicated loop leave a stray reference to the wrong one?
Is `dayTotals` now a two-line composition of two single-purpose sums, or did the split stop halfway with one loop still doing both jobs under the other's name?
Do the two sums stay independent when an order contributes to only one of them - revenue with no flour, or flour with no revenue?
If a reviewer objects that this is now two passes over `orders` instead of one, is there an honest answer on hand, or just a shrug?
Would extracting `revenueCents` and `flourGramsUsed` further into `.reduce()` calls actually help here, or is that a different day's refactoring?
